stem: What is a process in PRINCE2?
answer: A structured set of activities that defines the sequence of actions and their inputs and outputs
distractors: A documented agreement between the project board and the project manager that sets the tolerances for a stage
A collection of management products that are baselined at the same point in the project lifecycle
The set of roles and responsibilities needed to direct, manage and deliver a project
A technique for estimating the cost and duration of a piece of work before it is authorized
A principle that must be applied continuously throughout the life of the project
A decision point at which the project board authorizes the project to move to the next stage, or stops it
explanation: A process is a structured set of activities defining the sequence of actions and their inputs and outputs to achieve a specific objective. Because PRINCE2 is a process-based approach, the seven processes together supply the activities needed to direct, manage and deliver a project.

stem: What do the seven PRINCE2 processes provide?
answer: The set of activities required to direct, manage and deliver a project successfully
distractors: The seven roles that must be appointed to every project board, whatever its size
The four management levels into which a project organization is divided
The principles that must be applied at every stage of the project
The management products that must be baselined in the project initiation documentation
The techniques used to tailor the method to the size of the project
The tolerances within which the project manager is permitted to operate
explanation: The manual describes PRINCE2 as having seven processes that provide the set of activities required to direct, manage and deliver a project successfully. Principles, practices, roles and management products are separate elements of the method, not what the processes themselves supply.

stem: What is the minimum number of stages a PRINCE2 project can have, and what must the first one be?
answer: Two stages, the first of which is the initiation stage
distractors: Two stages, the first of which is the final stage
Three stages: an initiation stage, at least one delivery stage and a final stage
One stage, covering initiation, delivery and closure together
Two stages, the first of which is a pre-project stage before initiation
Four stages: starting up, initiation, delivery and closure
Three stages, the first of which is a pre-project stage
explanation: The lifecycle in the process model figure always has at least two stages - an initiation stage and a final stage - with any number of stages in between. Starting up a project happens before the first stage, so it is not itself counted as a stage.

stem: What is the trigger that starts a PRINCE2 project, and who provides it?
answer: A project mandate, provided by the business that is commissioning the project
distractors: A project brief, provided by the project manager at the start of the project
A project initiation request, provided by the project board to the executive
A business case, provided by the executive to the board for approval
A statement of work, provided by the preferred supplier to the customer
A project initiation documentation, provided by the project manager to the board
A project product description, provided by the senior user to the manager
explanation: The trigger for a project is the project mandate, which the business provides; it can range from a verbal instruction to a fully justified project definition. The project brief is produced later, during starting up a project.

stem: What does starting up a project put in place before the project board decides whether to initiate the project?
answer: The management team is appointed, and a project brief and an initiation stage plan are produced
distractors: The project initiation documentation and the benefits management approach are produced
The business case is developed in full, and the first stage is authorized by the project board
The project mandate is written, and the project board tolerances are agreed with the business layer
The team plan and the first work packages are created for the delivery teams
The end project report is drafted, and the post-project benefits reviews are scheduled with the user
The communication management approach is agreed, and the project is closed by the board at the end
explanation: Starting up a project appoints the project manager and the project board and produces the project brief and a stage plan for the initiation stage. The full business case, the project management approaches and the project initiation documentation belong to initiating a project.

stem: Which process does the project board use to decide whether to proceed with project initiation?
distractors: Starting up a project
Initiating a project
Managing a stage boundary
Controlling a stage
Managing product delivery
Closing a project
explanation: The decision to proceed is taken by the project board through its own process, directing a project, after reviewing the project brief and the initiation stage plan. The board returns to that process at the end of initiation to authorize the project and the next stage.

stem: During the initiation stage, which process is used to plan the next stage in detail?
distractors: Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Controlling a stage
Directing a project
Managing product delivery
Closing a project
explanation: Initiating a project covers planning at the appropriate level, the project management approaches and controls, the business case and how benefits will be reviewed, but the detailed planning of the following stage is done through managing a stage boundary. That process is first used at the end of the initiation stage and then at the end of each subsequent stage except the final one, although it can also be used to prepare an exception plan at any time.

topic: Baseline of the project initiation documentation
stem: Why is the version of the project initiation documentation created during initiation kept rather than discarded once it has been updated?
answer: Because its content is expected to change under change control, so this version is the baseline
distractors: Because it becomes the end project report when the project closes, and is then filed by the manager
Because the business layer requires a copy before any stage can be authorized
Because it must be re-approved in full at the end of every stage, and then returned to the manager
Because it records the lessons that later projects are required to apply
Because it holds the only approved version of the project mandate, and the original business case
Because project assurance audits it at every stage boundary, and the board reviews the audit report
explanation: The manual notes that the contents of the project initiation documentation are likely to change throughout the project under change control, so the version produced during initiation is preserved as the original baseline against which later versions are reviewed. It is not an end-of-project report, and it is not re-approved in full at each boundary.

stem: During a delivery stage, how does progress information travel between the project manager and the board, and between the teams and the project manager?
answer: The project manager sends highlight reports to the board, and team managers send checkpoint reports to the project manager
distractors: The project manager sends checkpoint reports to the board, and team managers send highlight reports to the project manager
The project manager sends end stage reports to the board, and team managers send highlight reports to the project manager
The project manager sends highlight reports to the board, and team managers send end stage reports to the project manager
The project manager sends exception reports to the board, and team managers send issue reports to the project manager
The project manager sends highlight reports to the board, and team managers report only at the stage boundary
The project manager sends checkpoint reports to the board, and team managers send work package notices to the project manager
explanation: The board delegates day-to-day control to the project manager, who reports progress upwards through highlight reports, while team managers executing work packages report to the project manager through checkpoint reports. End stage reports are produced at the boundary, not as routine progress reporting during a stage.

stem: What does the project manager do towards the end of a stage in order to ask permission to proceed to the next stage?
answer: Report how the current stage performed, update the business case and plan the next stage in detail
distractors: Report how the current stage performed, re-baseline the project initiation documentation and release the team
Report how the current stage performed, close the project and schedule the benefits reviews
Update the business case, authorize the next stage and allocate the work packages
Plan the next stage in detail, appoint a new project board and revise the project mandate
Produce the end project report, archive the project documentation and release the resources
Prepare an exception plan, escalate the stage to the business layer and await a new mandate
explanation: At the end of a stage the project manager reports the stage's performance, updates the business case and plans the next stage in detail, giving the board what it needs to judge continuing viability. Authorizing the next stage is the board's decision, taken in directing a project, not something the project manager does.

stem: What must the project board be satisfied about before a project can close?
answer: That recipients can own and use each product and the business the project product
distractors: That every benefit in the business case has already been realized and measured
That all post-project benefits reviews have been completed and signed off
That the project has delivered within its original baseline for time and cost
That the project team has been released and the documentation has been archived
That the senior supplier has accepted the final work package
That the project mandate has been reissued for the next stage
explanation: Closure depends on the board being satisfied that recipients can own and use their products ongoing and that the business can take overall ownership of the project product. Most benefits are realized after the project, so the post-project reviews are only planned at closure rather than completed; archiving and releasing people are closure activities that follow the decision.

stem: Which management product sets out how and when post-project benefits reviews will happen, and who is responsible and accountable for them?
distractors: The business case
The end project report
The project initiation documentation
The communication management approach
The benefits realization plan
The project product description
explanation: The benefits management approach documents how and when post-project benefits reviews should occur and who is responsible and accountable for them. The business case records the justification and the expected benefits, but not the arrangements for reviewing them after closure.

stem: Which management levels are the PRINCE2 processes aligned with in the process model?
answer: The business layer, directing, managing and delivering
distractors: Corporate, programme, project and team
Directing, managing, delivering and assuring
The business layer, governing, managing and delivering
Portfolio, programme, project and delivery
Strategy, governance, management and operations
Directing, planning, managing and delivering
explanation: The process model aligns the processes with four management levels: the business layer, directing, managing and delivering. The triggers between the processes are also shown, with arrows to the business layer notifying the business of an update or request.

stem: Which of these is NOT part of the standard structure used to describe each PRINCE2 process?
answer: A schedule of the tolerances delegated to each team manager and the board
distractors: A purpose statement and the specific objectives the process is to achieve
A context description, including a table of inputs and outputs for each activity
A RACI table describing the responsibilities for the process
explanation: Each process chapter is structured around purpose, objectives, context, activities, responsibilities and the application of the practices within the process. Tolerances delegated to team managers belong to the plans and progress practices, not to the way a process is described.

stem: According to the key message closing the introduction to processes, how do the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 work together?
answer: The practices ensure that the principles are continually applied during the processes, suited to the project
distractors: The principles ensure that the practices are applied only at stage boundaries, when the board reviews progress
The processes ensure that the practices are tailored to each project, while the principles are applied only at the start
The practices replace the processes on small projects, where a full set of activities would be disproportionate
The processes take precedence over the principles wherever the two conflict, because they define the activities
The principles are applied by the business layer while the practices are applied by the delivery teams
The five elements are applied in sequence, starting with principles and ending with processes
explanation: The key message is that the five integrated elements work together: the practices ensure the principles are continually applied during the processes, in a way specific to the project context and taking account of people and groups in the project and organizational ecosystems. The elements are integrated, not applied in sequence or owned by separate layers.
